relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (hasNoRelationshipTo) - previously minted for Sync Gateway's channel/role model vs. server RBAC; same shape of explicit docs-stated disjointness applies here
relations.evidence: These credentials are separate from [organization roles](../organizations/organization-user-roles.md) and [project roles](../projects/project-roles.md). Your Capella user account's organization and project roles control your access to the Capella UI, while cluster access credentials control programmatic and application-level access to data.

relations.subject: capella:cluster-access-credential
relations.evidence: Cluster access credentials are specific to a cluster and consist of a cluster access name, password, and a set of access levels or roles, depending on the chosen credential type.

relations.subject: capella:cluster-access-credential

relations.evidence: You cannot convert basic access credentials to advanced access credentials, or advanced access credentials to basic access credentials.

notable_absence.finding: This page - despite being the batch's predicted authoritative home for cluster-level access control - never once uses requiresCapellaRole to gate anything on this page's own content. It explicitly declares cluster access credentials to be a SEPARATE system from the capella-role:* catalog (see hasNoRelationshipTo relation), and only cites Organization Owner/Project Owner very lightly, purely as pointers into the separate organization/project role pages, not as a gate this page itself defines. Cluster-rbac.md's only two named capella-role:* citations both come from its 'Managing Cluster RBAC'/'See Also' sections, which point OUT to manage-database-users.md and the org/project role pages rather than stating a role requirement in cluster-rbac.md's own prose - manage-database-users.md (this batch's next file) is where the actual Project Owner/Cluster Manager Prerequisites gate lives.

cross_component_finding: DIRECT TEST OF THIS BATCH'S HYPOTHESIS, RESULT: SURPRISE. cluster-rbac.md is NOT the authoritative page for the capella-role:* catalog at all - it names zero new roles and does not even restate the full 8-role catalog; 'Cluster Access' (its own title) refers to a completely different axis: the cluster-access-credential-type enum (Basic/Advanced) and the privilege model gating what a CREDENTIAL (not a user, not a capella-role) can do to data. The page opens by explicitly stating credentials are separate from organization/project roles. Bigger finding: this page IS the authoritative source for the privilege:capella-advanced-access-* family the registry describes as '11 named privileges' - and this page's own table lists 25 distinct privileges, not 11 (Global: Global Function Execute, Query Catalog, Global Function Manage, Analytics Read, Analytics Admin, Stats Read, Query Manage Catalog, Query Curl Access; Analytics: Analytics Manage, Analytics Select; Data: Data Read, Data Manage, Data Monitor; Eventing: Eventing Manage; Search: FTS Manage, FTS Read; Query: Query Insert, Query Update, Query Index, Query Read, Query Manage, Query Delete, Query Execute, Query Use Sequences, Query Manage Sequences). Only 10 of the registry's existing 11 privilege concepts match a row here by label (global-function-execute, global-function-manage, query-delete, query-execute, query-index, query-insert, query-manage, query-manage-sequences, query-read, query-update); the 11th registered concept, privilege:capella-advanced-access-scope-admin, does NOT appear anywhere in this table under that name - it isn't one of this page's 25 Advanced privileges at all (the closest match, `scope_admin`, is cited only as a Couchbase Server role backing the BASIC 'Write' access level, a different privilege model entirely). This is the same lesson as round 6's role catalog, replayed on the privilege side: a vocabulary assembled from scattered statement-page citations (11 items) undercounts the authoritative page's own catalog (25 items) by more than half, and the one item that WAS in the scattered vocabulary turns out to be miscategorized relative to this page's own two-tier (Basic-role vs. Advanced-privilege) model.
cross_product_finding: The 'Server Role' column of the Advanced-privileges table and the Basic Read/Write access-level table both map every Capella-side privilege/access-level onto named Couchbase Server RBAC roles (data_reader, data_writer, query_select, query_manage_index, analytics_admin, fts_admin, scope_admin, etc.) via direct links into server/current/learn/security/roles.md - confirming yet again (per the registry's rbac-role:role placeholder) that Capella's privilege/credential system is a thin management-plane wrapper around the exact same data-plane RBAC role vocabulary server/ uses; no new server-role names were found, only new CAPELLA-side privilege names wrapping already-known server roles.
